children: The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel brought record-setting rain and flash flooding to Las Vegas over the weekend. The rare weather event stranded motorists, disrupted access to many Strip resorts, and inundated roads as preparations continued for the city’s Formula One race in November.

Notably, Harry Reid International Airport recorded 1.08 inches of rain Sunday morning, breaking the previous record of 0.78 inches set in 2012. Across the broader region, some locations received 2 to 3 inches or more in less than 12 hours. Las Vegas Fire & Rescue conducted numerous swift-water rescues as floodwater and debris blocked roads.

For casinos, the clearest immediate impact was difficulty reaching properties rather than a shutdown of gaming operations. Road closures, stranded vehicles, and airport weather advisories may have discouraged some visits, although affected road closures had cleared by Monday and F1 preparations are back on track, according to local reporting.

title: Tropical storm remnants crash the party on the Las Vegas Strip
